label: Second copy step (first token fed back) in short sequences, plus t=0 on t/k
predicate: ((recall_idx == 1) & (L <= 4) & isin(in_tok, [tok("t"), tok("k"), tok("p"), 29, tok("b"), tok("g"), tok("r")])) | ((t == 0) & isin(in_tok, [tok("t"), tok("k")]))
explanation: Two regimes. (1) Most of the activation mass (~74%) is at step L+1 (recall_idx 1), where the first original token comes back in as input and the model outputs original token 1. The rate there falls off steeply with sequence length (L=3 highest, L=4 high, almost nothing for L>=6), and is much higher when the first token is t, k, p, 3, b, g or r. The largest activations (up to the max) are of this kind, e.g. "t x x <DEL> [t] x" and "p w x x <DEL> [p] w x". (2) At t=0 it fires on every sequence that starts with t or k, but only weakly (about 0.03-0.07 of max). This is about 53% of active steps but only about 21% of the mass. A small remainder sits at original positions 2-4 just before the delimiter (to_go 1-2) and on long sequences. It essentially never fires on the delimiter step, on copy steps after the second one, or at t=1. The predicate misses step-L+1 activations on other first tokens and on L=5, and adding those trades precision for mass recall: with all first tokens at L<=4, mass recall is about 0.95 but precision about 0.42.
